rows.title: Canada Signs New Deals With China After Trump Drops Trade Demand
rows.summary: After two days of talks in Vancouver with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, Canada signed three finance agreements with China covering cooperation between finance ministries, financial regulators and a joint central-bank working group, and both sides welcomed progress on a currency-swap arrangement and more market access in financial services. The talks came as Washington dropped a demand that would have given the U.S. final say over Canada's trade deals with other countries, while U.S. tariffs on lumber, steel, aluminum and autos remain unresolved. Canadian goods exports to China are up 41% so far in 2026, and Ottawa aims to lift exports to China by another 50% by 2030. The moves show a mid-sized, U.S.-dependent economy trying to diversify its trading partners to reduce risk, even as some barriers such as a 100% duty on Canadian canola oil remain.
rows.fact: Newsweek reports that Canada and China signed agreements linking their finance ministries, regulators and central banks, and pledged to pursue greater financial-services market access and a bilateral currency swap. It notes an existing arrangement keeping lower Chinese tariffs on Canadian canola meal, peas, lobster and crab runs to the end of 2028, and that Prime Minister Mark Carney is heading to the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
rows.outlook: A University of Alberta China Institute expert read the ministers' remarks as a sign Ottawa will keep deepening engagement with China, while a Canadian official said a U.S.-Canada deal is still some way off.
rows.why: 미국 의존도가 높은 캐나다가 관세 갈등 속에서 중국과 금융·무역 협력을 넓히는 모습을 통해 무역 다변화와 위험 분산의 원리를 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a U.S.-dependent economy like Canada responds to tariff conflict by diversifying trade and financial ties, illustrating the principle of spreading risk across partners.
rows.term_def: An agreement between two central banks to exchange each other's currencies, so businesses and banks can more easily get the other country's money for trade and investment, especially in a crisis.
rows.note: Fallback to a 7-day story: no major Canadian policy or top-tier data release in the last 24h had readable coverage (StatCan Sept manufacturing/wholesale came out Nov 13 22:30 KST with only thin FX-site coverage; statcan.gc.ca fetch was blocked). Newsweek body read in full; outcomes cross-checked against the Finance Canada release of Nov 9 (canada.ca). Not the excluded tariff-remission item (that is only mentioned in passing in the article).

opinion.title: Canada, China agree to 'enhance' financial services co-operation
opinion.author: Kevin Carmichael
opinion.summary: Kevin Carmichael's briefing says the second Canada-China Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue in Vancouver produced modest results, including only a vague promise to work on financial-services market access. In his 'Talking point' analysis, he argues the thin outcomes matter less than how seriously both sides treated the meeting. He notes China sent He Lifeng, one of Xi Jinping's most trusted lieutenants, while Canada fielded its finance and trade ministers backed by Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem and bank regulator Peter Routledge. He concludes that signed cooperation deals are notable given the two governments were barely speaking a couple of years ago.
opinion.why: 합의 내용 자체보다 '누가 협상에 나왔는가'가 경제 외교의 신호가 될 수 있다는 점을 보여주어 뉴스를 비판적으로 읽는 법을 배울 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches readers to look past headline promises and read who shows up at the table as a signal of how serious an economic relationship is becoming.

rows.title: US producer prices rise further in October
rows.summary: The US Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the producer price index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, a bit less than the 0.4% economists polled by Reuters had expected, after an upwardly revised 1.4% jump in September. Even so, prices were 6.5% higher than a year earlier, the biggest annual increase since November 2022. Goods prices climbed 0.5%, led by food and basic organic chemicals, while services prices rose 0.2% for a fifth straight month. Because producer prices measure what businesses charge each other, they often signal where consumer prices are heading, and the report came days after a hotter-than-expected consumer inflation reading. With the Federal Reserve's policy rate at 3.75%-4.00%, markets are debating whether the Fed will raise rates by a quarter or half point in December.
rows.fact: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October versus a 0.4% forecast, with September revised up to 1.4%, and the annual rate reached 6.5%, the largest in four years. Goods rose 0.5% and services 0.2%. The report followed a stronger-than-expected October CPI and a jobs report showing unemployment falling to 4.1%.
rows.outlook: Financial markets were split between a 25- and a 50-basis-point Fed rate hike in December, and CME's FedWatch tool showed another hike expected in January.
rows.why: 기업 간 거래 가격인 생산자물가가 소비자물가와 금리 결정으로 어떻게 이어지는지 이해하는 데 좋은 사례이기 때문이다.
rows.why_en: It shows how prices businesses pay each other feed into consumer inflation and into the central bank's interest-rate decisions.
rows.term_def: A measure of the average change in prices that producers receive for goods and services they sell, such as factory and wholesale prices; it is often an early signal of future consumer price changes.
rows.note: Last-24h official data release (BLS October PPI, released Nov 13 08:30 ET = 22:30 KST). Reuters dispatch read in full as republished by Devdiscourse (3 paragraphs); figures cross-checked with TT/Sweden Herald (0.3% m/m, 6.5% y/y, core 0.3% m/m, 5.0% y/y). CNBC and CNN versions could not be fetched.

opinion.title: Today's Wholesale Price Report Could Tip the Fed Toward a Half-Point Hike
opinion.author: Annika Masrani
opinion.summary: Written just before the release, this analysis explains why the October PPI mattered for whether the Fed lifts rates by a quarter or a half point in December. It notes forecasts of a 0.4% monthly rise after September's 1.3% surge, and points out that the annual rate was expected to climb partly because a weak reading from October 2025 dropped out of the 12-month comparison, a so-called base effect. The author highlights wholesale service prices such as healthcare and financial services because they feed into the PCE index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge. It also lays out how markets might react: a hot reading could lift Treasury yields and pressure tech stocks, while a soft one could pull yields lower; the actual 0.3% print came in on the softer side.
opinion.why: 하나의 경제지표가 금리 기대, 채권금리, 환율, 주가에 어떻게 연쇄적으로 영향을 주는지 보여 주기 때문이다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how one data release can ripple through interest-rate expectations, bond yields, currencies and stock prices.

rows.title: Korean economy continues to 'grow at solid pace': finance ministry
rows.summary: In its November Green Book, South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy upgraded its official view of the economy, saying it continues to grow at a solid pace on the back of surging exports, faster investment and gradually improving consumption. That is a step up from the 'recovery' wording the ministry had used for about a year. The upgrade rests heavily on October exports, which jumped 93.7% from a year earlier to a record $115.3 billion, mostly thanks to semiconductors. The ministry still warned that the Middle East war and high oil prices could hurt household livelihoods, and that jobs remain scarce for vulnerable groups: youth employment has fallen for 48 straight months. It promised to broaden the base for growth and to strengthen policies that reduce disparities so the gains are shared more widely.
rows.fact: The finance ministry's monthly Green Book, released Nov. 13, said the Korean economy 'continues to grow at a solid pace,' replacing its earlier 'recovery' assessment. It cited record October exports of $115.3 billion (up 93.7% year-on-year), inflation easing to 2.8% in October, and 139,000 more jobs, while noting that the number of employed people aged 15-29 fell by 196,000.
rows.outlook: The ministry sees the global economy growing moderately but flags uncertainty from Middle East developments and the direction of AI industry policy, and warns high oil prices could weigh on livelihoods.
rows.why: 정부가 경기를 공식적으로 어떻게 진단하는지, 그리고 반도체 수출 호황 속에서도 청년 고용과 물가 부담이 왜 남아 있는지 함께 이해할 수 있기 때문이다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a government officially judges the state of the economy, and why a chip-export boom can coexist with weak youth jobs and oil-price pressure on households.
rows.term_def: A monthly report from Korea's finance ministry that describes how the economy is doing; small changes in its wording, like moving from 'recovering' to 'growing at a solid pace', signal the government's view of the business cycle.
rows.note: Body read in full on Korea Times (free Yonhap republication, 2026-11-13 10:24 KST). Last-24h official government assessment (monthly Green Book). Yonhap English site could not be fetched (permission request timed out).

opinion.title: When the economic illusion fades
opinion.author: Cho Min-geun
opinion.summary: JoongAng Ilbo editorial writer Cho Min-geun argues that Korea's headline numbers, with growth rebounding toward 3% and inflation in the upper 2% range, rest on temporary props. He says a government fuel price ceiling, now in its eighth month, has kept inflation below 3%, an effect the Bank of Korea puts at about 0.6 percentage point, but its fiscal cost has grown to more than 5.6 trillion won with no exit plan. He also notes that chips account for 73% of this year's export increase and nearly half of exports, leaving the economy exposed if AI data center spending slows. Pointing to a widening gap between exports and domestic demand, pressure on autos from Chinese EVs and 'jobless growth' for young people, he urges policymakers to drop their complacency and prepare a plan B.
opinion.why: 좋아 보이는 경제 지표 뒤에 가격 통제와 반도체 쏠림 같은 취약점이 숨어 있을 수 있다는 점을 비판적으로 생각해 볼 수 있다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches readers to question strong headline statistics by showing how price controls and dependence on one industry can hide weaknesses.

rows.title: Eurozone Q3 GDP unchanged in second estimate as uneven growth clouds the outlook
rows.summary: Eurostat's second estimate, released on November 13, confirmed that the euro area economy grew 0.4% in the third quarter of 2026, the same as the preliminary reading but slower than 0.6% in the second quarter. Compared with a year earlier, output was up 1.3%, slightly faster than the previous 1.2%. The headline was lifted by Ireland, whose GDP jumped 5.5% on information-and-communication and manufacturing activity, a figure often distorted by multinational companies. The big economies were weak: Germany grew only 0.2%, Italy was flat and France shrank 0.1%. This uneven picture matters because the European Central Bank is fighting high inflation with rate hikes, and slower growth makes that job harder.
rows.fact: The second estimate left euro area Q3 GDP at +0.4% q/q and +1.3% y/y, unchanged from the flash print, which had beaten forecasts of about 0.2%. Ireland's +5.5% contrasted with Germany +0.2%, Italy 0.0% and France -0.1%.
rows.outlook: The author notes recent French and Spanish inflation data do not argue against another ECB rate hike next month and questions whether growth can hold up into Q4 and 2027 as the ECB may face weaker growth and higher inflation at the same time.
rows.why: 한 나라(아일랜드)의 다국적 기업 회계가 유로존 전체 GDP를 부풀릴 수 있다는 점과, 성장 둔화 속 물가를 잡아야 하는 중앙은행의 딜레마를 함께 이해할 수 있기 때문입니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how one small economy's multinational accounting can inflate a region's GDP headline, and the dilemma a central bank faces when it must fight inflation while growth weakens.
rows.term_def: Statistics agencies first publish a quick 'flash' GDP number using partial data, then a second estimate a few weeks later with more complete data; the number can be confirmed or revised.
rows.note: Last-24h official data release (Eurostat Q3 GDP second estimate, Nov 13, 2026). Article body read on investingLive; figures cross-checked with a Finimize brief (Nov 13), which also reports euro area employment flat q/q and +0.4% y/y. Eurostat's own release page blocked automated access.

opinion.title: Eurozone GDP: Strong headline, steady underlying growth
opinion.author: Bill Diviney, Aggie van Huisseling
opinion.summary: ABN AMRO economists argue that the 0.4% Q3 headline overstates the eurozone's strength because Ireland's volatile GDP jumped 5.5% after a 10% surge in Q2; excluding Ireland, growth was only about 0.2%. Consumption kept growing despite high energy prices, but the external sector weakened. Spain (+0.6%) and the Netherlands did well, while France contracted, Italy stagnated, and Germany's 0.2% gain relied mainly on government spending. They expect underlying growth of roughly 0.2-0.3% per quarter with no meaningful pickup in 2027 because of high energy prices and rising interest rates.
opinion.why: 발표된 숫자(헤드라인)와 실제 경제 체력(기조적 성장)을 구분해 읽는 법을 배울 수 있는 분석입니다.
opinion.why_en: It teaches how to separate a flashy headline number from an economy's underlying growth trend.

rows.title: China's October new bank loans shrink for third time this year as credit demand weakens
rows.summary: Data released by the People's Bank of China on Friday showed new yuan loans fell by 100 billion yuan in October, the third monthly contraction this year, when economists had expected a small 20 billion yuan increase. Households cut their borrowing (including mortgages) by about 430 billion yuan and companies by 160 billion yuan, while outstanding loan growth slowed to a record-low 4.7% and M2 money supply growth eased to a 19-month low of 7.1%. October is seasonally weak because of the week-long national holiday, but lending over the first ten months was still far below last year, showing that targeted credit support and a 'moderately loose' monetary stance have not yet revived private investment or household spending. Broader total social financing rose slightly faster, to 7.2%, because government bond issuance is doing more of the work that bank loans used to do. For the world economy, weak Chinese borrowing means soft domestic demand in the second-largest economy, leaving growth more dependent on exports.
rows.fact: New yuan loans shrank by 100 billion yuan in October versus a forecast gain of 20 billion, with both household and corporate loans contracting. Outstanding loan growth fell to a record-low 4.7% year on year and M2 growth slowed to 7.1%, while total social financing growth edged up to 7.2% on government bond issuance.
rows.outlook: ANZ's Zhaopeng Xing expects full-year growth above the 4.5% floor of the target and says new policy steps are unlikely soon because the central bank is prioritizing exchange-rate stability.
rows.why: 금리를 낮추고 돈을 풀어도 가계와 기업이 빚을 내려 하지 않으면 경기 부양 효과가 약해진다는 '신용 수요' 문제를 세계 2위 경제의 실제 데이터로 이해할 수 있다.
rows.why_en: It shows with real data from the world's second-largest economy that easy monetary policy has limited power when households and firms simply do not want to borrow.
rows.term_def: A broad measure of all the money flowing to China's households, companies and government in a period, counting not just bank loans but also bonds, stock sales and other financing.
rows.note: Body read via WebFetch (Reuters text republished by The Standard); release date Friday Nov 13, 2026 confirmed by an FX.co data note timestamped 2026-11-13. Official PBOC data release in the last 24h. China's October activity data (industrial output, retail sales, FAI) and Japan's Q3 GDP are not out yet (due Nov 16 KST).

opinion.title: China's Banking Problem of Unwanted Credit
opinion.author: Nicholas Larsen
opinion.summary: Larsen argues that China's weak lending reflects a lack of demand, not a lack of money: strategic industries, state-linked firms and some exporters still borrow, but households and many private firms are paying down debt amid the property slump. Even with corporate loan rates around 3% and mortgage rates near 3.1%, borrowing has not revived, which suggests expectations about income, sales and asset values matter more than small rate cuts. He warns that pushing banks to lend anyway could weaken loan standards and create future bad loans, noting household nonperforming loans hit a record 2.22 trillion yuan in 2025. While accepting the central bank's view that financing is shifting toward bonds and equity, he concludes the lasting fix lies outside banking: stronger household incomes, better pensions and unemployment protection, finishing unbuilt homes, and fairer treatment of private business.
opinion.why: '돈을 싸게 빌려줘도 빌리지 않는' 현상이 왜 생기는지, 그리고 통화정책보다 소득과 사회안전망이 왜 중요한지를 알려준다.
opinion.why_en: It explains why cheap money fails to spark borrowing and why incomes and social safety nets can matter more than monetary policy.
